## The idea

Everyone in our cohort has epilepsy. Think of epilepsy as appearing when a person's total **liability** (genetic plus everything else) crosses a threshold. A person with a strongly damaging rare variant is pushed most of the way by that variant alone, so they need little polygenic risk to cross. A person with no such variant needs more.

So **inside a case-only cohort**, people whose epilepsy is explained by a single rare variant should, on average, have a **lower** epilepsy PRS than people without one. By changing which genotype group plays the "case" and which the "comparison", we can ask several questions with the same scores.

**Write the hypotheses down before running anything.** With several groups and eight thresholds it is easy to keep looking until something is significant. These are ours, with the expected direction:

| | Case group | Comparison group | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 (main) | No variant reported | Monogenic | higher PRS |
| H2 | VUS only | Monogenic | higher PRS (a VUS usually does not explain the epilepsy) |
| H3 | Incomplete-penetrance genes | High-penetrance genes | higher PRS (these variants need more help) |
| H4 (exploratory) | Missense | PTV, in high-penetrance genes | higher PRS (missense often milder) |
| Negative control | all of the above, with the **height** PRS | | no difference |

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
source("config.R")
source("R/functions.R")
```

## 1. Put everything together

```{r}
groups <- read_tsv(file.path(RESULTS, "cohort_groups.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
pcs    <- read_tsv(file.path(RESULTS, "pcs.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
scores <- read_tsv(file.path(RESULTS, "prs_scores.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

dat <- scores %>%
  inner_join(pcs, by = "IID") %>%
  inner_join(groups, by = "IID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex)) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with(c("epilepsy_Pt_", "height_Pt_")), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)), .names = "{.col}_z"))

# the main scores: at the threshold chosen in advance, in standard deviations
dat <- dat %>% mutate(epilepsy_z = .data[[score_col(dat, "epilepsy", PT_MAIN)]],
                      height_z   = .data[[score_col(dat, "height", PT_MAIN)]])

cat(nrow(dat), "people in the analysis\n")
count(dat, dx_status)
```

The scores are **standardised** (mean 0, SD 1 across the cohort), so a difference of 0.3 means "0.3 standard deviations".

## 2. H1, step by step

First, look:

```{r, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4.5}
plot_groups(dat, case = dx_status == "No variant reported", control = dx_status == "Monogenic",
            title = "H1: epilepsy PRS")
```

Then the model. We regress the PRS on group membership, adjusting for sex and the first PCs:

```{r}
h1_data <- dat %>% filter(dx_status %in% c("No variant reported", "Monogenic")) %>%
  mutate(group = as.integer(dx_status == "No variant reported"))
fit <- lm(epilepsy_z ~ group + sex + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4, data = h1_data)
summary(fit)$coefficients["group", ]
```

`compare_groups()` does exactly this and returns one tidy row, which makes it easy to run many comparisons:

```{r}
compare_groups(dat, case = dx_status == "No variant reported", control = dx_status == "Monogenic", name = "H1")
```

**Reading it.** `diff_SD` is how much higher the PRS is in the case group, in SD; `low` and `high` are its 95% confidence interval. Is the direction the one we predicted?

## 3. All the planned comparisons

```{r}
planned <- bind_rows(
  compare_groups(dat, dx_status == "No variant reported", dx_status == "Monogenic", name = "H1 No variant vs monogenic"),
  compare_groups(dat, dx_status == "VUS only", dx_status == "Monogenic", name = "H2 VUS only vs monogenic"),
  compare_groups(dat, gene_group == "Incomplete penetrance", gene_group == "High penetrance",
                 name = "H3 Incomplete vs high penetrance"),
  compare_groups(dat, variant_class == "Missense" & gene_group == "High penetrance",
                 variant_class == "PTV" & gene_group == "High penetrance", name = "H4 Missense vs PTV")
)
planned %>% mutate(P_bonferroni = pmin(P * n(), 1)) %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 2)))
```

We tested four hypotheses, so a strict correction multiplies each P by 4 (Bonferroni).

**Your turn 1.** Which hypotheses are supported? Which comparison is too small to say much? (Look at `n_case` and `n_control`, and the width of the interval.)

## 4. The negative control

Same comparisons with the height PRS. We expect nothing.

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
negative <- bind_rows(
  compare_groups(dat, dx_status == "No variant reported", dx_status == "Monogenic", prs = "height_z", name = "H1 No variant vs monogenic"),
  compare_groups(dat, dx_status == "VUS only", dx_status == "Monogenic", prs = "height_z", name = "H2 VUS only vs monogenic"),
  compare_groups(dat, gene_group == "Incomplete penetrance", gene_group == "High penetrance", prs = "height_z",
                 name = "H3 Incomplete vs high penetrance"),
  compare_groups(dat, variant_class == "Missense" & gene_group == "High penetrance",
                 variant_class == "PTV" & gene_group == "High penetrance", prs = "height_z", name = "H4 Missense vs PTV")
)
forest_plot(bind_rows(planned, negative)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(epilepsy_z = "#B2182B", height_z = "#7F7F7F"),
                      labels = c("Epilepsy PRS", "Height PRS (negative control)"))
```

## 5. Why we adjust for PCs

Run H3 with and without the PCs:

```{r}
bind_rows(
  compare_groups(dat, gene_group == "Incomplete penetrance", gene_group == "High penetrance",
                 covariates = "sex", name = "H3, sex only"),
  compare_groups(dat, gene_group == "Incomplete penetrance", gene_group == "High penetrance",
                 name = "H3, sex + PCs")
) %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 2)))
```

**Question.** Why does the estimate change? (Hint: notebook 3, which gene sat in the smaller ancestry cluster?)

## 6. Sensitivity: every threshold

The main result uses `PT_MAIN`, chosen in advance. Here we check that the conclusion does not depend on that choice. This is a check, **not** a way to pick the best-looking threshold.

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
by_threshold <- lapply(PT_LEVELS, function(pt) {
  compare_groups(dat, dx_status == "No variant reported", dx_status == "Monogenic",
                 prs = score_col(dat, "epilepsy", pt), name = format(pt))
}) %>% bind_rows()

ggplot(by_threshold, aes(factor(contrast, contrast), diff_SD)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), colour = "#B2182B") +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, as.numeric(contrast) == PT_MAIN), size = 4, shape = 21, fill = NA, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "GWAS P value threshold", y = "Difference (SD)", title = "H1 at every threshold",
       subtitle = "Circled: the threshold fixed in advance") + theme_workshop()
```

## 7. Do we have enough people?

A quick power estimate: with these group sizes, what difference could we detect 80% of the time?

```{r}
detectable <- function(n1, n2, power = 0.8) {
  n_eff <- 2 / (1 / n1 + 1 / n2)   # equivalent size of two equal groups
  power.t.test(n = n_eff, power = power, sig.level = 0.05, alternative = "one.sided")$delta
}
planned %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(detectable_SD = round(detectable(n_case, n_control), 2)) %>%
  select(contrast, n_case, n_control, diff_SD, detectable_SD)
```
